details:
Obviously, devs are concerned about mods for some reason, and it's likely profit and/or investment and/or safety and/or complaint related.
Obviously, the user base depends on mods for QOL and filling gaps that Devs are unable to fill quickly (for whatever reason, which can be another discussion entirely).
So, seeing as the concern revolves around some mods being harmful, why not a whitelist of accepted mods? This can be
- a page on their site
or
- choosing a community site after review
or
- Moving to steam workshop compatibility (difficult, but massive signal to community)
If the workshop option isn't used, a method could concevibly be in place to check loaded mods against this white list, and allow them through. If a mod isn't on the whitelist, Devs can choose to block or restrict access until the offending mod is removed, OR throw up a warning message about the mod being potentially risky.
If Devs implement this in a way thats fair, and makes sense. People will happily work within the framework provided.
As it stands, the other alternative is for VRC to make a complete 180 from current history and be hyper aggressive about QOL updates. Unfortunately, at this point, that action could very easily lead to allegations of just copying work that modders had done already.
title: Mod support that makes everyone happy
